Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:1:1.hebrew: אבל אכלה שית שנין כו' - הקשה ר"י בר מרדכי: אפי' לא אייתי סהדי אלא דאכלה שלש שנין, יהא נאמן לומר "לקחתיה קודם מינך", במיגו דאי בעי אמר "מינך זבינתה"? ואומר ר"י דאין זה מיגו, דמעיקרא לא יטעון כלל "מינך זבינתה", דאין יודע אם יש לזה שטר שקנאה ממנו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:1:1.english: But if he consumed [the produce] for six years, etc. - Rabbi Yitzchak ben Mordechai asked: Even if [the possessor] brought witnesses only that he consumed [the produce] for three years, he should be believed to say, "I bought it before [I bought it from] you," by virtue of a *migo* — for if he wished, he could have said, "I bought it from you"? But Rabbi Yitzchak says that this is not a *migo*, because at the outset he would not claim at all, "I bought it from you," since he does not know whether this [other party] has a deed showing that he acquired it from him.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:2:1.hebrew: אמר רבה מה לו לשקר - רבה גרסינן, דאביי ורבא אמרי לקמן (בבא בתרא דף לג:) דלא סבירא להו הא דרב חסדא, דמה לי לשקר במקום עדים לא אמרינן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:2:1.english: Rabbah said: Why would he lie? - We read "Rabbah," for Abaye and Rava say below (Bava Batra 33b) that they do not hold this [principle] of Rav Chisda, [and that the argument] "why would I lie" we do not apply where there are witnesses.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:3:1.hebrew: מה לי לשקר במקום עדים לא אמרינן - תימה לרשב"א: אמאי הוי במקום עדים? נימא: של אבותיו היתה יום אחד, ונאמר שלקחה מאבותיו, דהא טוענין ליורש! ומהימנינן ליה בהא דקאמר שאבותיו דרו בו יום אחד, במיגו דאי בעי אמר: מינך זבנתיה. ולקמן נמי, דקאמרי נהרדעי דהיכא דאמר "של אבותי שלקחוה מאבותיך" דחוזר וטוען — הא אפילו לא יטעון שלקחוה, אלא אמר שדרו בה יום אחד, אנן טענינן ליה! ואומר רבינו יצחק דשל אבותי משמע שהיתה מעולם של אבותי, ולא שלקחוה עד שיפרש בדבריו. ולקמן דנקט "שלקחוה" — לא שצריך שיטעון שידע שלקחוה, אלא "של אבותי", שראיתי שדרו בה יום אחד, על כן אני רוצה לזכות, דשמא לקחוה אבותי במשפט, וטוענין ליורש:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:3:1.english: "What reason do I have to lie?" — we do not say [this] where there are witnesses - Rashba found this astonishing: Why is this a case of [contradicting] witnesses? Let us say: It was his fathers' for one day, and let us say that [his fathers] bought it from [the claimant's] fathers, for we argue on behalf of an heir! And we believe him in this, when he says that his fathers lived in it for one day, by virtue of a migo: for if he wished, he could have said, "I bought it from you." And below as well, where the Nehardeans say that when he said, "It is of my fathers, who bought it from your fathers," he may retract and make a [new] claim — but even if he does not claim that they bought it, and says only that they lived in it for one day, we argue on his behalf! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that "of my fathers" implies that it was of my fathers from time immemorial, and not that they bought it, unless he specifies so in his words. And below, where [the Gemara] says "that they bought it," it is not that he must claim that he knows they bought it; rather [he says], "It is of my fathers," because I saw that they lived in it for one day, and therefore I wish to establish my right, for perhaps my fathers took it by [a court] ruling — and we argue on behalf of an heir.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:7:1.hebrew: ומודו נהרדעי היכא דאמר שלקחוה כו' - מספקא לר"י: היכא דנפיק לבראי וחזר ואתא לב"ד, אי מצי למימר הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 31a:7:1.english: "And the Nehardeans agree where he said, 'that they bought it,' etc." - Ri was uncertain: where [the defendant] went outside and returned to the court, whether he is able to say this.
